title: Singareni explores partnerships with US Firms for Critical Minerals and Data Centres
excerpt: HYDERABAD: A high-level delegation led by Meredith Metzler, Political and Economic Chief of the US Consulate General in Hyderabad, met with Singareni Collieries Company Limited (SCCL) Chairman and Managing Director Dr. Buddhaprakash Jyoti at Singareni Bhavan on Friday to discuss joint partnerships in the critical minerals sector, pumped storage power, and data centre infrastructure. Critical […]HYDERABAD: A high-level delegation led by Meredith Metzler, Political and Economic Chief of the US Consulate General in Hyderabad, met with Singareni Collieries Company Limited (SCCL) Chairman and Managing Director Dr. Buddhaprakash Jyoti at Singareni Bhavan on Friday to discuss joint partnerships in the critical minerals sector, pumped storage power, and data centre infrastructure. Critical minerals and geoscience The CMD explained that SCCL, leveraging its mining experience, has ventured into the critical minerals sector and is exploring joint ventures and technological collaborations with several countries. The US delegation highlighted opportunities for collaboration with American companies in the sector. They expressed interest in SCCL's recently established Geo-Science Laboratory at Kothagudem and the potential for extracting Rare Earth Elements (REEs) from the overburden of open-cast mines. The CMD noted that the company is seeking foreign investments and partnerships with technology and research institutions, and the US representatives invited SCCL to a Critical Minerals Conference in the United States in April. Data centres and power With the rapid growth of Artificial Intelligence, the US representatives said they were exploring locations for data centres in Telangana, noting that adequate water and uninterrupted power are essential. SCCL officials proposed establishing Pumped Storage Power Plants at several locations using its worked-out open-cast mines to provide reliable power to data centres, particularly during peak hours. They noted these could be developed through suitable investments and partnerships, with water potentially sourced from the nearby Godavari River. The US Consulate representatives noted that several American companies have already set up data centres in Telangana and that the infrastructure in the Singareni region offers favourable conditions for such investments. The CMD invited the delegation to visit Singareni's mines and the Geo-Science Laboratory. The meeting was attended by Srimali Kari and Shibha Tripathi, Political and Economic Specialists, and Sunil Kumar, Commercial Specialist, from the US Consulate. From SCCL, Director (Projects and Planning) K. Venkateswarlu, General Manager (Marketing and Coordination) T. Srinivas, General Manager (Business Development) K. Ramadasu, General Manager (Exploration) Pankaj Kulshreshtha, General Manager (Power Projects) Guru Prasad, and other senior officials participated. ]]>

title: From IPL Teams to Everyday Users, Mumbai’s Baller Athletik Brand Is Betting on Infrared Recovery Sleepwear, Hits 15k+ Users
excerpt: Training intensity, speed, and strength receive considerable attention when it comes to athletes, but their ability to recover between sessions is equally important to sustaining performance over time. A 2023 systematic review published in Sports Medicine - Open, which examined 25 studies on sleep interventions among athletes, found that extending nighttime sleep and taking naps were among the most effective approaches reviewed for improving sleep and physical or cognitive performance, although the authors acknowledged limitations in the available evidence. The importance of recovery, however, extends well beyond the demands of competitive sport. Sleep is fundamental to everyday health and functioning, and the awareness of its importance is gradually improving as well. “We have successfully applied recovery-focused technology in clothing, and aim to take the conversations about deep rest beyond training grounds and into everyday life. Customers have reported better sleep duration and quality within just one week of wearing our sleepwear. This is a first for the Indian market,” Tanveer Daswani, founder of Baller Athletik, tells Startup Pedia in an exclusive interview. Founded in 2019 and based in Mumbai, Baller Athletik is a performance and recovery apparel brand built on infrared sciences. It offers sleepwear and activewear engineered to help users recover faster and sleep deeper, and has catered to 15,000+ customers to date. The backstory of the Baller Athletik founder Originally from Mumbai, Tanveer is currently 44 years old. After pursuing a BBA degree from Bentley University, he moved to England, where he took his first job with Imperial Tobacco, selling cigarettes door to door. He subsequently moved to Nigeria in West Africa, joining a family business in the tobacco trade that operated across wholesale, semi-wholesale, and retail channels. “It was one of the hardest things to sell, so I did learn a lot. But also, there was a bit of a cognitive dissonance because I was deeply invested in fitness myself. My day job and my values didn’t align,” he says. In 2012, despite having no prior experience in the sector, Tanveer established a specialized military uniform business in Nigeria, catering to the military, police, and air force, with products and technologies spanning vector protection, visual camouflage, flame and heat protection, stealth, and ballistic technologies. “I would talk to military personnel and be impressed by the emphasis placed on discipline, physical conditioning, and recovery within the armed forces. A lot goes into maintaining the soldiers’ performance and readiness, both in terms of financial resources and other investments. This was when I discovered the Far Infrared (FIR) technology and its application in performance wear, and its direct impact on human physiology" the startup founder shares with Startup Pedia. By collaborating with research labs in Europe, Tanveer was able to build and sell FIR-infused military textiles. But when Nigeria experienced a major financial crisis in 2014-15, everything came crashing down. The currency was repeatedly devalued, and the textile business was washed out. “My wife and I had a baby on the way. We decided to return to Mumbai, India, after spending approximately 20 years abroad. I had to rebuild everything from scratch,” the entrepreneur says. The journey and challenges of building Baller Athletik from the ground up In India, Tanveer Daswani identified sports as an industry where performance and recovery technology could find early acceptance. He drew inspiration from how sports science and advanced performance technologies are first developed and used at elite levels, such as Formula 1, before becoming more accessible to the wider market. In 2019, he established Baller Athletik (previously known as Baller Recovery) with patient capital (undisclosed) raised from foreign investors. He did make 50-60 calls to venture capitalists in India, but was met with skepticism around the new category. “I partnered with a manufacturing unit in Mumbai and made some recovery wear infused with the Far Infrared technology. The next step was to have high-performance athletes validate the products and understand whether the technology worked for them and, if so, to what extent,” the startup founder mentions. The Rajasthan Royals marked the brand’s first major breakthrough in 2019, when the players wore Baller Athletik’s infrared clothing for sleep and recovery. Later, following a sports-agnostic approach, the brand also worked with the Bengaluru Warriors and U Mumba of the Pro Kabaddi League and ATKMB in the ISL. These elite sports partnerships helped the team gather crucial feedback and make necessary changes to the final product. “Athletes would monitor their performance and then their recovery and sleep scores. Each time, they would report better recovery than before. My thesis was simple: if what we had built at Baller Athletik was working for these players with intense schedules, then the value proposition would most definitely work with corporate professionals, health-conscious individuals, and just about anyone who understands the metric of recovery and how it binds with their cognitive and physical function," Tanveer Daswani explains. While 2019-2020 went into early validation, it was in 2021 that Baller Athletik’s D2C website went live in the market. Initially, the recovery products accounted for just 5% of the website’s assortment, with activewear and performance wear taking the larger chunk. But since the COVID-19 pandemic propelled health, rest, and recovery to larger, everyday conversations, sleep subsequently became an additional focus area. With this shift, Baller Athletik gradually began building a stronger positioning around recovery wear. Baller Athletik: The Invisible Advantage Today, Baller Athletik operates as a performance and recovery apparel brand built on infrared sciences. It offers sleepwear and activewear engineered to help users perform better, recover faster, and sleep deeper. It describes its mission as “creating scientifically backed, high-functioning apparel that supports athletes, professionals, and everyday movers.” The current product portfolio includes: Activewear Recovery wear Athleisure Sleep-focused products The prices range from Rs 995 to Rs 1,900, with the brand operating in the mid-premium segment. The founder claims the current average order value is Rs 3,000-3,500. But what truly differentiates Baller Athletik’s apparel? What is the science that goes behind it? And does it retain even when the clothes are washed? Firstly, it makes sense to explain Far Infrared (FIR). It is the radiation that is part of the electromagnetic spectrum and is associated with the radiant heat emitted by warm objects, including the human body. “We know that FIR is a naturally occurring form of energy linked to the body’s metabolic activity. Our proposition centers on using this very energy in clothing to support recovery,” startup founder Tanveer Daswani says. Baller Athletik’s development team incorporates a proprietary matrix of bioceramic minerals into the fabrics used for its sleepwear, performance wear, and athleisure. These minerals contain oxides of aluminium, silicon, and other elements, selected for their far-infrared-emitting properties. Unlike wearable electronic devices, the technology is integrated into the fabric itself, so the wearer does not need to attach a separate device. The technology works through a mechanism: the bioceramic material absorbs some of the body’s emitted heat and re-emits energy in the far-infrared range. The company says its products have been tested for outcomes including balance, reaction time, blood circulation, and muscle recovery, and its website features athlete testimonials reporting improvements in fatigue, soreness, and sleep. Even after 100+ washes, the bioceramic-infused fabrics continue to function the way they are intended to, without any reduction in effectiveness. Tanveer tells Startup Pedia that all of the brand’s garments undergo laboratory testing to verify the presence of bioceramic minerals and their far-infrared-emitting properties. Additionally, Baller Athletik reports working with European sports and performance laboratories to investigate efficacy in performance and recovery. The performance and recovery apparel brand has been associated with athletes from top sports teams such as Rajasthan Royals, UMumba, ATK Mohun Bagan, and Bengal Warriors, along with institutions like NSCA and IIS. Currently, Baller Athletik is the official recovery partner of Gujarat Titans. “The reported apparel industry return rate is 33%. You know ours? It is under 3%. Users have reported having better sleep within just days of using our sleepwear,” Tanveer affirms. Growth and what’s next for Baller Athletik With a team size of 15 full-time employees, the performance and recovery apparel brand works out of its Mumbai office. The founder did not disclose the specific revenue but says Baller Athletik is growing at 24% month-on-month. The team has catered to 15,000+ customers to date. By December 2026, Baller Athletik plans to launch in the UAE and UK, expanding its performance and recovery apparel offering to international markets. Additionally, Tanveer Daswani is exploring B2B opportunities across corporate wellness, hospitality, and travel, identifying potential applications for Baller Athletik’s recovery-focused apparel beyond individual consumers. These include sleepwear for hotel guests, premium sleepwear for first- and business-class passengers, and corporate wellness solutions aimed at improving employees’ sleep and recovery. “Every time someone asks me who my ideal customer is, I tell them it is anyone who sleeps. Sleep remains a very under-researched function of the human body, and there is so much that scientists are discovering every day. It is complex, after all. But at Baller Athletik, we want to make recovery something that people look forward to, simply because they know they will wake up feeling better the next day and be ready for whatever lies ahead. The end goal is to build a global performance and recovery company,” he signs off. FAQ Q. When was Baller Athletik founded? A. Baller Athletik was founded in 2019. Who is the founder of Baller Athletik? Tanveer Daswani is the founder of Baller Athletik. What does Baller Athletik do? Baller Athletik is a performance and recovery apparel brand using infrared technology to support recovery and sleep. What is the revenue of Baller Athletik? While Tanveer did not disclose revenue, he claims 24% month-on-month growth and over 15,000+ customers to date.
